k6parity_pairing_interpretation_rules: both operands replay through the shared BF16 head (the ladder does this by construction), so head width drops out: turboderp's rung has no exl3 K6 head and the head term alone is ~+0.000127, a third of the plausible margin
the MTP draft bytes are free: the fidelity protocol never engages MTP, so the 0.3057 GiB draft asymmetry is byte accounting only, already excluded from both body figures

the CALIBRATION CORPUS is the real confounder: turboderp calibrates on his own data, K6-parity on exllamav3's standard_cal_data -- identical widths and identical body bytes still leave two different Hessians. A turbo6-vs-k6parity delta therefore conflates allocation shape with calibration content until the alt-calibration condition (local://altcal-handover.md, runs before saka/awq in my window) bounds the content term: inside the +/-2.9e-05 converter-draw envelope the pairing is clean; at 1e-04 a delta of that size says nothing about allocation. The turbo6 body-parity SENTENCE is therefore written only after the alt-cal bound is known

the question is different from K6-parity's own: theirs was whether spending Q6_K's byte surplus closes a cross-engine gap (it does, 0.001634 MATCHES); this one is whether at the same body bytes and the same engine a hand-designed non-uniform allocation beats a uniform one -- no cross-engine floor term, so the cleaner comparison. If turbo6 wins, that is evidence against our allocation shape and gets published as loudly as the EDA negative was

the 17.0537 GiB body figure is MEASURED on the k6parity side, not predicted: SixteenFlipCalib2 re-derived it from the realised manifest (23,035,310,148 B payload minus embedding/head/vision/draft = 18,311,299,648 B), predicted-to-the-byte
